topPRs.title: feat(template): add SetFeeVaultConfig for in-place fee-vault config updates
topPRs.author: donoso-eth
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds a reusable `SetFeeVaultConfig` template that updates the on-chain config
(recipient / withdrawalNetwork / minWithdrawalAmount) of one or more L2 fee-vault
predeploys **in place**, via the vaults' own owner-gated setters
(`setRecipient` / `setWithdrawalNetwork` / `setMinWithdrawalAmount`), sent as
`OptimismPortal2.depositTransaction` from the L1 ProxyAdminOwner. No proxy upgrade,
no re-initialize. Chain-specific values come from `config.toml`.

## Why

The existing fee-vault templates change the recipient by **upgrading the impl**
(`UpdateFeeVaultRecipient` installs a new immutable impl; `FeeVaultUpgradeTemplate`
migrates to the storage design via `initialize`). Once a chain's vaults are already on the
storage design (e.g. OP Sepolia / Ink Mainnet: L1FeeVault v1.6.1, OperatorFeeVault v1.1.1),
re-running `FeeVaultUpgradeTemplate` reverts (`InvalidInitialization`) and would downgrade
the impl. On those chains recipient/network/min are mutable storage with owner-gated
setters, so a plain setter call is the correct, minimal mechanism — which is what this
template provides.

### Files

- **`src/template/SetFeeVaultConfig.sol`** — `L2TaskBase` template; emits one portal
  deposit per *changed* field across the configured `vaultProxies`.
- **`test/tasks/example/sep/041-set-fee-vault-config/`** — example task (OP Sepolia:
  L1FeeVault + OperatorFeeVault → shared recipient, WithdrawalNetwork.L1).
- **`test/integration/SetFeeVaultConfigIntegration.t.sol`** — end-to-end test; forks
  L1 + OP Sepolia, replays the setter deposits, asserts the vault config changed. Reuses
  `IntegrationBase`.

### Validation

- **Capability/version gate** — rejects vaults below the min version that exposes the
  setters (Sequencer/Base/L1 ≥ 1.6.0, Operator ≥ 1.1.1); old immutable vaults must use
  `FeeVaultUpgradeTemplate` first.
- **Required `l2RpcUrls` preflight** — asserts `L2 ProxyAdmin.owner() == aliased root`,
  enforces the version gate, and **dry-runs the setters** as the aliased owner so an L2
  revert surfaces at setup instead of silently on relay.
- **Per-field skip-unchanged** — only fields that differ from live state produce a deposit;
  at least one must change (else the framework reverts "No actions found").
- **`_validate`** — asserts action count + every action targets the OptimismPortal, value 0.
- Non-zero recipient, `network <= 1`, and known-vault checks.

## Test plan

- [x] `forge test --match-test test_setFeeVaultConfig_integration -vvv` — 1/1 passed (4/4 deposits succeed; recipient/network/min verified on the OP Sepolia fork)
- [x] `just simulate` on `sep/041` — `SETFEEVAULTCONFIG: VALIDATED PORTAL DEPOSIT ACTIONS`
- [x] `forge build --deny-warnings` — clean
- [x] `forge fmt --check` — clean
- [x] `./src/script/check-struct-order.sh` — clean

## Self-review (template-review checklist)

Ran the internal template-review checklist; **0 blocking findings**. Minor items resolved:
inline interfaces (`IOptimismPortal2`/`IProxyAdminView`/`IVersioned`), `vm.label`s, corrected
NatSpec (the "No actions found" behavior + skip-unchanged sign-time semantics), removed an
unused import, `Supports:` line added. `_taskStorageWrites = ["OptimismPortalProxy"]`
cross-checked against the sim state diff.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Escalation:** this is a **new template type** and performs a **cross-layer** operation
> (L1→L2 portal deposits driving L2 setter calls) — flagged for **Security-team review** per
> the template-review checklist.

## Notes

- Additive: does not modify `UpdateFeeVaultRecipient` or `FeeVaultUpgradeTemplate`.
- No `Regression.t.sol` entry: per-field skip-unchanged reads live L2 state, so a
  hardcoded-calldata regression test would be non-deterministic. The `sep/041` example is
  covered by CI's `simulate-all-templates`, and the integration test covers the end-to-end
  L2 effect — matching the sibling `UpdateFeeVaultRecipient`, which likewise has no
  regression test.

topPRs.title: feat: Ink SystemConfig owner transfers to FoundationOperationsSafe (eth/055, sep/101)
topPRs.author: Wazabie
topPRs.body:
## Description

Transfers ownership of the Ink `SystemConfigProxy` on both networks from the current Ink-controlled owner Safe to the Optimism **FoundationOperationsSafe**, using the existing `TransferSystemConfigOwnership` template (one chain per task):

| Task | Chain | SystemConfigProxy | Current owner (signer) | New owner (FOS) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `eth/055-ink-transfer-system-config-owner` | Ink (57073) | [`0x62C0a111929fA32ceC2F76aDba54C16aFb6E8364`](https://etherscan.io/address/0x62C0a111929fA32ceC2F76aDba54C16aFb6E8364) | `0xBeA2Bc852a160B8547273660E22F4F08C2fa9Bbb` | [`0x9BA6e03D8B90dE867373Db8cF1A58d2F7F006b3A`](https://etherscan.io/address/0x9BA6e03D8B90dE867373Db8cF1A58d2F7F006b3A) |
| `sep/101-ink-transfer-system-config-owner` | Ink Sepolia (763373) | [`0x05C993e60179f28bF649a2Bb5b00b5F4283bD525`](https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0x05C993e60179f28bF649a2Bb5b00b5F4283bD525) | `0xBeA2Bc852a160B8547273660E22F4F08C2fa9Bbb` | [`0x837DE453AD5F21E89771e3c06239d8236c0EFd5E`](https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0x837DE453AD5F21E89771e3c06239d8236c0EFd5E) |

### Input verification

- Current owners verified on-chain: `cast call <SystemConfigProxy> "owner()(address)"` returns `0xBeA2Bc852a160B8547273660E22F4F08C2fa9Bbb` on both networks (the same 3-of-5 Safe, v1.3.0, identical owner set on both networks).
- `SystemConfigProxy` addresses verified against the superchain-registry ([mainnet/ink.toml](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/blob/main/superchain/configs/mainnet/ink.toml), [sepolia/ink.toml](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/blob/main/superchain/configs/sepolia/ink.toml)).
- New owners match `FoundationOperationsSafe` in `src/addresses.toml` (`[eth]` / `[sep]`).
- Signer Safe nonces pinned via `stateOverrides` (eth: 50, sep: 4 — on-chain values at task creation) so the VALIDATION.md hashes are reproducible.

### Simulation

Both tasks simulate successfully (`just simulate` and `just simulate-stack`): the only state changes are the `SystemConfig` owner slot (`0x33`) flipping to the FOS and the signer Safe nonce bump. Domain hashes were additionally reproduced independently with `cast keccak` (see each VALIDATION.md).

Note: `just simulate-stack sep 101-...` currently fails in unrelated task `097-osaki-l1-ownership-transfers` — its pinned FoundationUpgradeSafe nonce (70) has drifted behind the live value (72) on main. The sep/101 single-task simulation passes.

## Harness fix: EIP-7702 delegated EOA owners

On **mainnet**, one owner of the Ink Safe (`0x6a0A93Cd6d6FB7a36bF6234ef4650Bf9474e7682`) is an EIP-7702 delegated EOA: its code is the 23-byte delegation designator `0xef0100…`. `MultisigTask` classified any owner with code as a child Safe and called `nonce()` on it, which reverts (the delegation target exposes no Safe interface) — making every task signed by this Safe impossible to simulate.

This PR adds `Utils.isEip7702DelegatedEOA` (exact designator check: 23 bytes, `0xef0100` prefix) and excludes such owners from:
- the owner-Safe nonce safety checks in `_overrideState`, and
- the Safe branch of `_incrementOwnerNonce` (account nonce is used instead, as for any EOA).

Covered by a new unit test (`test_isEip7702DelegatedEOA`); `vm.etch` itself rejects malformed designators, so only valid designators can exist on-chain. The eth/055 simulation exercises this path end-to-end against live mainnet state. Other `code.length > 0` owner-classification sites (`isNestedSafe`, `_collectAllSiblingDataToSign`) are nested-task-only and not hit by these tasks; they can be hardened in a follow-up.

### Testing

- `test/libraries/Utils.t.sol`: 13/13 pass (includes new 7702 test)
- `test/tasks/MultisigTask.t.sol`: 21/21 pass
- Remaining fork suites fail locally only with `historical state is not available` from the public RPC — identical failures on unmodified `main` (verified via `git stash`); CI archive RPCs are authoritative.

## Checklist

- [x] Simulation completes successfully (no reverts) — single-task for both; stacked for eth
- [x] State changes reviewed and documented in each VALIDATION.md
- [x] README.md complete for both tasks
- [x] VALIDATION.md with domain/message/safe-tx hashes for both tasks
- [x] Task status set to DRAFT, NOT READY TO SIGN
- [x] No TODOs left in task files

topPRs.title: eth/062: Ink Mainnet fee-vault recipient update (Gelato → OPE, fee vault recipient)
topPRs.author: Wazabie
topPRs.body:
## Ink Mainnet Migration — fee-vault fast follow (eth/062)

Adds `eth/062-ink-fee-vault-recipient-update`: transfers Ink Mainnet's (chainId 57073) two cost-covering fee vaults to the OP Enterprise **fee vault recipient**, as the post-cutover fast follow of the Gelato → OPE migration (plan step 15 / W33; not on the 2026-07-28 cutover critical path).

| Vault | Change |
|---|---|
| `L1FeeVault` (`0x…001a`, v1.6.1) | recipient `0xa6f0F94C…6c93` → `0x1eB630b2e7409597D462dd5f3D21E305FC56B8C9` |
| `OperatorFeeVault` (`0x…001b`, v1.1.1) | recipient `0x…0019` (BaseFeeVault) → same cost recipient; withdrawalNetwork **L2 → L1** |

`SequencerFeeVault` / `BaseFeeVault` are untouched (chain-governor revenue). Min withdrawal amounts unchanged. Exactly **3 portal deposits** (per-field skip-unchanged).

Numbered `062`: next free slot after the merged migration tasks `eth/060` / `eth/061` (#1490). The rollback contingency tasks (#1493) renumber after this.

### Recipient provenance
`0x1eB630b2e7409597D462dd5f3D21E305FC56B8C9` is the Ink Mainnet **fee-recipient** L1 EOA (Google KMS key ring `ink-mainnet-0`, key `cost-recipient`), deployed 2026-07-17. Source of truth: `k8s-netchef-prod` → `manifests/ink-mainnet-0/mn-ink-mainnet-0-op-signer/mn-ink-mainnet-0-op-signer.yaml` (auth entry `mn-ink-mainnet-0-cost-recipient`, chainID 1). It funds Ink's L1 operating costs (batcher / proposer / challenger top-ups).

### Status: DRAFT, NOT READY TO SIGN — three gates
1. **Stacked on #1504** (this PR's base branch): the task uses the new `SetFeeVaultConfig` template — post-Karst the vaults are on the setter design, so this is an in-place config update (no impl deploys; `FeeVaultUpgradeTemplate` would revert `InvalidInitialization` on these vaults).
2. **Governance:** signed by the L1PAO (nested 2-of-2 Foundation Upgrade Safe + Security Council) → requires the Ink chain-servicer-migration Maintenance Upgrade proposal to clear its veto window.
3. **Ordering / nonces:** pins account for both merged migration tasks — `eth/060` is FOS-signed (no effect on these safes); `eth/061` is L1PAO-signed (+1 each). Pins = live 2026-07-20 values (36/62/60) + 1 → L1PAO=37 / FUS=63 / SC=61. Re-simulate + regenerate hashes on any drift.

### Verification performed
- Live state (2026-07-20, `rpc-gel.inkonchain.com`): vault versions 1.6.1 / 1.1.1, current recipients/min/network as documented in config comments; L2 ProxyAdmin owner = aliased L1PAO (`0x6B1B…C4E3b`).
- `just simulate council` + `just simulate foundation`: template pre-flight (owner assertion, version gate, setter dry-run) passes; 3 deposits built, selectors/args verified (`setRecipient` `0x3bbed4a0` ×2, `setWithdrawalNetwork` `0x307f2962`).
- `just simulate-stack eth 062-… council|foundation` (what CI runs): both green; domain/message hashes match VALIDATION.md; root L1PAO safe tx hash identical on both paths.
- `check-task-statuses.sh` / `check-task-names.sh` pass.

topPRs.title: ci: pin isNestedTask fork to the task's FORK_BLOCK_NUMBER
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested via [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C03N11M0BBN/p1784723711347979)_

## Summary

**Before:** each example task's simulation already forks at its pinned `FORK_BLOCK_NUMBER` (from the task's `.env`), but the `isNestedTask` routing pre-check in `src/script/simulate-task.sh` always forked at the latest block. That pre-check is block-dependent — it resolves the task's root safe and calls `getOwners()`, treating the task as nested only if every owner is a contract — so probing at latest could route a task inconsistently with the pinned state its own simulation runs against. Forking at latest also raced load-balancer replica lag in CI: [job 202767](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/28803/workflows/0ed8cad7-998c-4ec3-a4ae-1eddf146e227/jobs/202767) (2026-07-22) failed with `failed to get block for block number: 46460537; latest block number: 46460536`.

**After:** the pre-check sources the task's `.env` and uses the same `_get-fork-block-args` helper as the simulation itself, so pinned tasks probe at their pinned block. Tasks without a pin are unchanged (still fork at latest).

---

## Additional context

Scope: this removes the replica-lag failure mode for pinned tasks only. Plain RPC endpoint timeouts (the other 3 attempts in the failed run) are infra-side and unaffected.

---
